chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Majilawayh narrated to me from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Huzaifa ibn Mansur, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'How many times have you performed Hajj?' I said: 'Nineteen.' He said: 'Indeed, if you had completed twenty-one Hajjs, you would be like one who visited Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him).'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward equivalent of visiting Imam Husayn?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) establishes the immense spiritual merit of Ziyarat al-Husayn by comparing it to the cumulative reward of twenty-one Hajjs, highlighting the unique status of the Imam of the Time in Shia piety. This comparison underscores the concept that visiting the shrine of the martyr of Karbala carries a weight comparable to multiple obligatory pilgrimages to the Kaaba, reflecting the deep emotional and theological connection Shia Muslims maintain with the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 37.  Imam  Ja’far  Sadiq  (a.s.)  asked  Huzaifa  bin  Mansur, “How many times have you performed the Hajj?” “Nineteen times,” he replied. Imam said, “If you perform it twenty-one times you would be like one who does the Ziyarat of Imam Husain Ibne Ali (a.s.) once.”
